assertion: The U.S. Census Bureau announced on September 15, 2026 that real median household income was $87,460 in 2025.
warehouse_value: $80,424 (2024, ACS 1-Year, simple average across states -- a different survey, not a recomputation of the same measure)
independent_value: $87,460 for 2025, up 2.6% from $85,210 in 2024, per Census press release CB26-151 and the underlying report 'Income in the United States: 2025' (P60-289)

sources.title: U.S. Census Bureau Newsroom: Income, Poverty and Health Insurance Coverage in the United States: 2025 (CB26-151)

table: census.acs1_income (context only; does not carry the CPS ASEC series the claim is based on)
sql: SELECT year, avg(median_household_income) AS avg_state_median FROM census.acs1_income WHERE year IN ('2019','2021','2022','2023','2024') GROUP BY year ORDER BY year
reason: The claim is drawn word-for-word from the Census Bureau's own press release, which was fetched and read directly. AskAmerica's warehouse has no CPS ASEC table and no 2025 income data of any kind, so the $87,460 figure cannot be independently recomputed from this corpus; it is verified instead by direct primary-source retrieval, which matches exactly.
